truth.statement: The orchard is not of no particular scientific interest. The survey that said so rested on four short visits in the driest fortnight of August, while the shed holds an unbroken notebook record from 1911, one hundred and fourteen years in nine hands, in which bloom moves eleven days earlier and no October bloom has ever been written down. What makes the case believable is the care with which the record was kept.
truth.question: Is the orchard really of no particular scientific interest, and what can show otherwise?

n08c2.event: Jonah sorts the notebooks by hand and sees the hands form a relay with clean changeovers.

n08c3.event: Jonah waits forty minutes outside the council office, listing what to tell Raval.

n08c4.event: Jonah and Mrs Cassar carry two bags of hive records up the hill in silence.

n08c5.event: Tobe explains the spreadsheet to Ada, who gets it once he calls it a ledger.

n08c6.event: Jonah stares at the chart and finds its smoothness troubling.

e08_0.event: Jonah sends the chart alone; it is admired and filed and the deadline passes.

e08_1.event: Jonah's guessed 1920s figures fail when Faulks finds three wrong dates.

n09d0.event: Raval says she can accept data with a clear method, a named keeper and a way to check it.

n09d1.event: Dr Abara offers two pages on cold air flow if the frost pocket is read at dawn for six weeks.

n09d2.event: Mrs Okonkwo drafts a custody note proving an unbroken chain of care.

n09d3.event: Mrs Cassar dates her method changes to the month, giving three clean periods.

n09d4.event: Tobe lists the four objections Faulks would make, all fair.

n09d5.event: The local paper offers a front-page photo of Ada with the notebooks.

n09d6.event: Jonah can formally request the developer's survey data, but the reply takes twenty working days.

n09d7.event: Ada recalls her grandmother's only story of 1917: a farm group horse kept in the old barn.

n09d8.event: Jonah signs to book the school hall for the term and takes responsibility.

e09_0.event: The lovely photo of Ada runs on page five while the deadline passes.

e09_1.event: Jonah publicly says the survey was written to order and every honest point is tainted.

n10d0.event: Two thermometers arrive and a dawn rota fills with Tobe, Mrs Cassar, Ada and Jonah.

n10d1.event: The formal data request is filed and acknowledged with a case number.

n10d2.event: Jonah writes the three-page method section, the hardest writing of all.

n10d3.event: Jonah writes four letters to the living families of notebook writers.

cq_payoff_did_ask_whether_notebooks_site.event: With Ada's October bloom margin beside him, Jonah reads the survey data as weather the notebooks never saw.

n10d4.event: Mrs Okonkwo brings the 1917 parish box that may explain the missing volumes.

n10d5.event: The reporter presses; Jonah must decide when the story runs.

n10d6.event: The objection form has one name line; Ada, eighty-one, has signed the notebooks six thousand times.

n10c0.event: Jonah stands in the frost pocket at dawn; Tobe does nineteen of the forty-two readings.

n10c1.event: Twenty working days against a six-week window leaves only two weeks to study the data.

n10c2.event: Dr Abara returns the first method draft marked with one word: why.

n10c3.event: Jonah posts the four letters at the bottom of the hill.

n10c4.event: Jonah is left alone with the brittle 1917 parish box.

n10c5.event: The frost chart goes up beside the bloom chart; frost later, bloom earlier.

n10c6.event: Ada says she will sign when there is something worth signing.

e10_0.event: The unchecked dossier goes online, is praised by four hundred readers and answered by no one with power.

e10_1.event: Jonah sends the numbers without a method and Raval rejects them.

n11d0.event: The developer's survey data proves thin: four visits, one transect, twenty-two species, site dry.

n11d1.event: Tobe's rain records show the visits fell in the driest days of that August.

cq_payoff_did_find_who_wrote_site2.event: Recalling the name D. Faulks he wrote in Ada's book, Jonah sharpens his answer to Halvor.

n11d2.event: Ada adds fourteen species to the survey's list from memory but will not swear to them.

n11d3.event: A September 1917 receipt shows two orchard books lent to the farm group and never returned.

n11d4.event: Jonah traces the farm group to the old market hall and its cellar card index.

n11d5.event: Jonah answers Tobe's four objections in writing; the fourth still needs facts.

cq_payoff_did_find_who_wrote.event: Knowing the name D. Faulks, Jonah refuses to let the deadline decide and aims at the driest fortnight.

n11d6.event: Dr Abara agrees to read the dossier once, properly, before endorsing it.

n11d7.event: Raval cannot help an objector but explains what the board will look for.

n11d8.event: Halvor from the developer buys Jonah a coffee and asks what would make him stop.

e11_0.event: The developer offers a saved corner and a plaque for Ada, but not the Bramley row.

e11_1.event: Jonah's letter attacking Faulks is published and the argument becomes about him.

n12d0.event: The visits, rain log and method all show the survey was done in a dry spell.

n12d1.event: Jonah reaches the market hall cellar, whose card index notes two borrowed books in 1917.

n12d2.event: A proper species list needs May, and it is November.

n12d3.event: Jonah weighs his honest answer to Halvor: nothing would make him stop.

n12d4.event: The short frost series is weak but shows the site has unmeasured microclimates.

n12d5.event: Jonah weighs whether to ask Ada, eighty-one, to speak before forty people.

n12d6.event: Jonah weighs releasing the dossier early or late.

n12c0.event: In the market hall basement Jonah works the card index in the dark between timer clicks.

n12c1.event: Jonah reads the rainfall record twice: the survey fell in the driest two weeks.

n12c2.event: Walking the rows in November, Jonah can be sure of only nine species.

n12c3.event: The coffee goes cold between Jonah and Halvor, who pays for it on the way out.

n12c4.event: Ada tells Jonah the hard part of speaking is the kindness afterwards.

n12c5.event: Jonah numbers and sources every page of the dossier and prints it at school.

n12c6.event: Jonah finds the two 1917 notebooks in a WAR COMMITTEE MISC box, in the 1943 pencil hand.

e12_0.event: Jonah quietly puts the found volumes back on the shelf and tells no one.

e12_1.event: The deadline decides; the unfinished version goes in and Jonah wishes he had tracked down the author.

n13d0.event: The full objection goes in: 114 years of dates, method, custody note, nine species, a cover sentence signed by Ada.

n13d2.event: A public hearing will force Faulks to defend his survey aloud.

n13d3.event: Ada and Tobe disagree on giving the developer the dossier before the hearing.

n13d4.event: The two war volumes and the receipt go into the dossier, closing the gap.

n13d5.event: Dr Abara will attend the hearing and say only what she can defend.

n13d6.event: Mrs Cassar packs thirty years of counts and a 1998 frame in a glass case.

n13d7.event: Jonah weighs having Ada read one 1947 page aloud at the hearing.

e13_0.event: The objection is accepted and the survey ordered redone in May by a new assessor.

e13_1.event: A checked typed copy of the 114 years is lodged with the archive.

e13_2.event: Reading the dossier, Jonah sees the notebooks are a chain of care across nine hands.

n14d0.event: Jonah answers the panel's first question with the rainfall record.

n14d1.event: Jonah answers the amateur charge with the custody note, double typing and marked doubts.

n14d2.event: Jonah tells the panel first that the frost series is short.

n14d3.event: Faulks explains his standard August survey and his pause reveals the wrong conditions.

n14d4.event: Ada reads her March 1947 page and the room falls silent.

n14d5.event: Jonah gives the file to the panel, developer and public on the same day.

n14c0.event: The hearing runs an hour late and the waiting steadies Jonah.

n14c1.event: The bloom and frost charts stand on the easel all afternoon.

n14c2.event: The note taker writes Abara's phrase long unbroken local series.

n14c3.event: Every panel member handles Mrs Cassar's 1998 frame.

n14c4.event: After Ada finishes reading, the room is silent for eight seconds.

n14c5.event: Waiting in the hall again, Mrs Cassar tells Jonah about a 1994 swarm.

e14_0.event: Jonah answers a fair question as unfair and the chair becomes careful.

e14_1.event: Jonah answers six questions with proof and one honest no; the officer asks for a growing-season resurvey.

n15d0.event: The officer's report cites the bloom chart, custody note and frost readings and drops the no-interest phrase.

n15d1.event: Permission comes with three conditions: May survey, winter frost study, series lodged with the archive.

n15d2.event: The spine road could move forty metres east at a cost.

n15d3.event: Jonah weighs whether the archive, the trust or the shed should keep the notebooks.

n15d4.event: Jonah gives the class that typed the 1930s an honest account.

n15d5.event: Jonah keeps the dawn readings going so the short series becomes long.

n15d6.event: Halvor asks again and Jonah now says he only wants the orchard to carry on.

e15_0.event: The notebooks go to the archive by deed of gift, Ada keeping the right to read them.

e15_1.event: The road moves forty metres east and the Bramley row stands.

e15_2.event: Dr Abara tells Jonah the October bloom was a question and the notebooks the answer.

n16d0.event: A winter dawn rota of nine people goes on the shed door.

n16d1.event: Ada teaches the old hands to new readers.

n16d2.event: The trust decides to look after both the notebooks and the trees.

n16d3.event: Jonah writes his first evening entry in a new notebook.

n16c0.event: Jonah buys a second thermometer for eleven pounds.

n16c1.event: The rota replaces the chart on the shed door and changes hands through January.

n16c2.event: Jonah reads the 1917 volumes; one line notes the horse returned in good shape.

n16c3.event: The May resurvey finds sixty-one species including a new fern.

e16_0.event: Jonah writes the hundred and fifteenth year, badly but faithfully.

e16_1.event: The December readings stop for eleven days and leave a permanent gap.

n17d0.event: The resurvey report recommends monitoring rather than clearing.

n17d1.event: Jonah counts the costs: strained friendships, a bad letter, Ada's tiredness.

n17d2.event: Jonah would do it all again except what he said about Faulks.

n17d3.event: In April the whole row, the big Bramley included, blossoms on time.

e17_0.event: The orchard is protected by a hundred and fourteen ordinary evenings of record.

e17_1.event: Jonah understands a record is the reason to be believed, not proof.

e18_0.event: Jonah indexes the six shelves for the first time.

e18_1.event: The next October is ordinary, the road runs east, and Jonah writes the last picking day.

e18_2.event: Jonah rereads the eleven words in his exercise book the day the resurvey report arrives.

e18_3.event: The notebooks are archived and closed; the series ends in the year of the hearing.
